rules_text:
Rules summary Objective Navigate the labyrinth to collect all treasure shown on your cards. Taking a Turn On your turn perform the following 2 actions in order: Shift the Maze: Take the tile outside the maze and place it at the end of any row or column marked with an arrow. Rotate the tile to desired position. Push the tile into the board, forcing the tile on the other end to be ejected from the maze and becoming the next tile played. Note: You cannot place the tile in the same spot it was ejected from in the previous turn. That is, you can't "undo" the previous move, even if you rotate the tile before inserting it. If player(s) were on the ejected tile, place the player(s) on the tile that is on the opposite end of where they exited Move Your Piece Move your piece to any desired tile along any open, continuous path. You may also choose to remain in place. If you end your turn on the same tile as the treasure card in front of you (opponents cannot see your treasure cards), Reveal the treasure card and look at the new treasure card on the top of your stack. Game End The person who collects all their treasure and returns to their starting point first wins!

---

Labyrinth (formerly The aMAZEing Labyrinth) has spawned a whole line of Labyrinth games. The game board has a set of tiles fixed solidly onto it; the remaining tiles that make up the labyrinth slide in and out of the rows created by the tiles that are locked in place. One tile always remains outside the labyrinth, and players take turns taking this extra tile and sliding it into a row of the labyrinth, moving all those tiles and pushing one out the other side of the board; this newly removed tile becomes the piece for the next player to add to the maze.

Players move around the shifting paths of the labyrinth in a race to collect various treasures. Whoever collects all of his treasures first and returns to his home space wins!

Labyrinth is simple at first glance and an excellent puzzle-solving game for children; it can also be played by adults using more strategy and more of a cutthroat approach.
community_text:
[Rating: 2/10] Would be a good children's/teaching game for spatial reasoning.  Otherwise, there is little decision making to be found.

[Rating: 2/10] This kind of fell short for me. Once someone has found all their treasures, then everyone knows where they have to go (back to their start spot) So the person taking the turn before them just has to avoid giving them a piece they can win with (or a maze position they can win with). I finally ended the game on purpose because I saw no end in sight.

[Rating: 2/10] Not much going on here - mostly the luck of the card draw with some very minimal blocking and bluffing to avoid being blocked. Clever board design with some tiles glued in place, though.

[Rating: 2/10] Ranking: :star::nostar::nostar::nostar::nostar:  One of my favorite games as a child. Played it again recently. Wish I didn't.

[Rating: 2/10] Even as a child I found this game boring and too simple. The sliding board is an interesting concept, but there just isn’t any real game here. After a few moves you’ve already seen everything it has to offer
